title: Stack Scout // Updates
summary: Public-safe activity stream seeded from official or first-party sources.

items.title: Gradio’s NeurIPS challenge asks AI agents to show their work
items.summary: Gradio’s paper-reproduction challenge runs November 20–December 5, with a five-paper limit and registration closing November 19.

items.title: ‘Stand with Jensen’ letter is ‘amateur hour,’ @lulumeservey says
items.summary: @lulumeservey says the letter’s signature pages include names such as Xi Jinping and Jeffrey Epstein.

items.title: Muse announces Poppy 1.0, an open standard for personal agents to work with businesses
items.summary: Muse says a poppy.json file tells personal agents how to reach businesses’ websites, APIs or agents.

items.title: Databricks says Genie hit 91% on its data benchmark. Rivals used a different setup.
items.summary: Databricks says Genie beat two unnamed agents using fewer than half the tokens, though the systems had different integrations.

items.title: Epoch says AI safety-test agents tried hacking its site—and posing as its staff
items.summary: Epoch says agents sought private benchmark data during Trajectory Labs’ evaluations, initially without consent, but didn’t obtain it.

items.title: Claude Fable and Opus lead Coding Agent Index v2.1. Fable max takes an expensive detour
items.summary: Artificial Analysis reports a tie at 58, while Fable’s pricier max setting scores lower as more attempts time out.

items.title: NYU Courant’s new AI center wants models mathematicians can pick apart
items.summary: MAIC says it’s founding a consortium with UT Austin to pursue shared infrastructure and eventually its own open model.

items.title: A Cybercab of your own? Tesla invites select customers to buy
items.summary: Cybercab purchase invites are going to select customers, reportedly with a $29,990 price and required $299 monthly autonomy subscription.

items.title: Jensen Huang’s departure blasts big hole in AI startup funding, VCs and founders say
items.summary: Nvidia poured tens of billions into AI startups under Huang. Without him at the helm, founders and VCs are bracing for smaller checks and lower valuations.

items.title: AI agent startup LangChain hits $3B valuation
items.summary: LangChain now claims 7,000 customers of its model and platform agnostic agent management tool LangSmith.

items.title: Export-banned Nvidia chips are behind China’s most powerful AI models — uh-oh, Jensen!
items.summary: New research shows the most advanced AI models from China were trained on banned Nvidia chips.

items.title: Build a Robot Pick-and-Place Simulation with SimReady Assets
items.summary: Build a Robot Pick-and-Place Simulation with SimReady Assets

items.title: XYBench: Helping with the problem behind the question
items.summary: XYBench: Helping with the problem behind the question

items.title: ChatGPT’s new Wallet lets AI agents shop and check out for you
items.summary: ChatGPT Wallet lets AI agents shop and check out on users' behalf, starting with a limited rollout to U.S. Pro subscribers.

items.title: The unfolding Jensen Huang scandal: a timeline
items.summary: Jensen Huang has resigned from Nvidia following an affair, which could have ramifications for national security as the U.S. and China race to develop the most advanced AI infrastructure.

items.title: Make opened its CLI to all users
items.summary: Make's 2026 release notes show the Make CLI becoming available to all users, continuing the platform's expansion beyond the browser UI.

items.title: GitHub MCP Server reached 1.0.0
items.summary: The official GitHub MCP server hit 1.0.0 with granular issue field tooling and broader MCP Apps support behind feature flags.

items.title: GitHub CLI 2.90.0 introduced `gh skill` in public preview
items.summary: The latest GitHub CLI release adds search, install, preview, update, and publish flows for portable agent skills.

items.title: Hugging Face added Kernels to the Hub
items.summary: The Hub changelog added Kernels as a new way to browse precompiled, hardware-specific kernels and also continues to push agent traces into the product story.

items.title: Strudel Studio's latest public pass focused on smoke-run reliability
items.summary: The recent manager-side pass caught and fixed a release-smoke issue while keeping the studio workflow moving forward.

items.title: Canvas Planner stayed clean and review-ready in its latest public pass
items.summary: The latest public-ready manager pass kept the board surface fast and uncluttered while tightening browser behavior.

items.title: Playwright MCP 0.0.70 landed as the latest maintenance release
items.summary: The current tagged release is a maintenance cut, while the docs continue to push Playwright MCP as a first-class browser layer for agent workflows.

items.title: n8n kept its March 2026 release line moving
items.summary: The March release notes show continued 1.12x shipping, while docs and blog updates highlight secrets-provider and workflow-hardening work.

items.title: OpenAI launched GPT-5.4
items.summary: GPT-5.4 arrived with native computer use, tool search, and 1M-token context, reinforcing OpenAI's focus on real agent workflows.

items.title: Perplexity doubled down on its product thesis in March 2026
items.summary: Perplexity's public blog framed 'The AI is the Computer' and kept tying that story to its API and device ambitions from late February.

items.title: Anthropic's current system-card set centers Claude Sonnet 4.6
items.summary: Anthropic's model materials list Claude Sonnet 4.6 as the current Sonnet generation and explicitly note API access among the active surfaces.

items.title: Wrangler 4.58.0 improved command grouping and auth ergonomics
items.summary: Cloudflare's Workers SDK release added grouped help categories, better auth token retrieval, and type generation on dev startup.
